name: Aegisaur
author: James Wyatt
pageNumbering: viewer pages, counted from the cover. Base stat block pages are printed folios.
section: An Ixalan Bestiary, Scales, Spikes, and Hammers
secondaryCrossCheck: 5etools indexed statistics checked against the named 2014 rules print sources.
appearanceEvidence: p. 28 describes shell-like armored scales and a bony tail club. Bellowing Aegisaur shows the broad, low armored body and colorful neck scales.
habitatEvidence: p. 28 groups Aegisaur with armored Ixalan plains herbivores. Grassland is the editorial search equivalent.
creditedArt: Craig J. Spearing, Bellowing Aegisaur, p. 28.
sourceDistinctions: The 2014 print gives +7 to hit. The numerical attack bonus follows print.

name: Aerosaur (Large)
author: James Wyatt
pageNumbering: viewer pages, counted from the cover. Base stat block pages are printed folios.
secondaryCrossCheck: 5etools indexed statistics checked against the named 2014 rules print sources.
appearanceEvidence: p. 29 describes leathery-winged reptiles, including pterodons and sunwings. A crested beak is visible in Shining Aerosaur. The gliding pose and palette are original portrait choices.
habitatEvidence: High perches and coastal updrafts are both named on p. 29. Ixalan coast is the editorial search tag for the coastal setting.
creditedArt: Dan Scott, Shining Aerosaur, and Johann Bodin, Sky Terror, appear on p. 29.
sourceDistinctions: Large is the catalog’s relative form label. The Quetzalcoatlus rules classify it as Huge.
The printed Dive Attack adds damage without naming a separate damage type.

name: Altisaur
author: James Wyatt
pageNumbering: viewer pages, counted from the cover. Base stat block pages are printed folios.
section: An Ixalan Bestiary, The Rumbling Herds
secondaryCrossCheck: 5etools indexed statistics checked against the named 2014 rules print sources.
appearanceEvidence: p. 27 groups Altisaurs with enormous long-necked herbivores. A four-legged build and powerful tail follow the Brontosaurus model. The pose and pigments are original.
habitatEvidence: p. 27 places Altisaurs on the Sun Coast plains and in sparse forests where they browse the tops of trees.
creditedArt: Keep any existing Altisaur book art reference and credit.
sourceDistinctions: The Ixalan text assigns the same Brontosaurus base to Altisaurs and Brontodons. This entry keeps the Altisaur name and setting description.
